t:
Section 10 of such Act is amended to read as follows:


“use of the mails and instrumentalities of interstate or foreign commerce
“Sec. 10. 
It shall be unlawful for any organization with respect to which there is in effect a final order of the Board determining it to be a Communist organization as defined in paragraph (5) of section 3 of this title, or for any person with knowledge or notice of such final order acting for on on behalf of any such organization—

“(1) 
to transmit or cause to be transmitted, through the United States mails or by any means or instrumentality of interstate or foreign commerce, any publication which is intended to be, or which it is reasonable to believe is intended to be, circulated or disseminated among two or more persons, unless such publication, and any envelope, wrapper, or other container in which it is mailed or otherwise circulated or transmitted, bears the following, printed in such manner as may be provided in regulations prescribed by the Attorney General: ‘Disseminated by _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _,’ (with the name of the organization in lieu of the blank) ‘an organization determined by final order of the Subversive Activities Control Board to be a Communist- _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ organization’ (setting forth in lieu of the blank whether action, front, or infiltrated, as the case may be); or


“(2) 
to broadcast or cause to be broadcast any matter over any radio or television station in the United States, unless such matter is preceded by the following statement: ‘The following program is sponsored by _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _,’ (with the name of the organization in lieu of the blank) ‘an organization determined by final order of the Subversive Activities Control Board to be a Communist- _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _organization’ (setting forth in lieu of the blank whether action, front, or infiltrated, as the case may be); or


“(3) 
to use the United States mails or any means, facility, or instrumentality of interstate or foreign commerce, including but not limited to radio and television broadcasts, to solicit any money, property, thing, or service, unless such solicitation if made orally is preceded by the following statement, and if made in writing or in print is preceded by the following written or printed statement: ‘This solicitation is made for or on behalf of _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ (with the name of the organization in lieu of the blank) ‘an organization determined by final order of the Subversive Activities Control Board to be a Communist-_ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ organization’ (setting forth in lieu of the. blank whether action, front, or infiltrated, as the case may be)

fable.w: The tempting reading is that this is purely a criminal prohibition and labeling mandate on Communist organizations, with the Subversive Activities Control Board and the Attorney General both inside the federal government, so no outside party takes part. However, the section authorizes the Attorney General to prescribe regulations governing how the required disclosure is printed, and under the definition a grant of rulemaking authority counts as participation even when it is incidental or discretionary. The call is uncertain because the rulemaking reference is brief and no explicit comment or hearing process is stated.
fable.s: printed in such manner as may be provided in regulations prescribed by the Attorney General

qwen_block.w: This section imposes a labeling requirement on organizations designated as Communist by a federal board. It does not require the federal government to consult with outside parties, hold public hearings, or coordinate with non-federal entities before making a decision. The interaction described is regulatory compliance by private entities, not participation in the decision-making process.
qwen_block.s: It shall be unlawful for any organization... to transmit or cause to be transmitted... any publication... unless such publication... bears the following... ‘Disseminated by... an organization determined by final order of the Subversive Activities Control Board to be a Communist... organization’

opus.w: The section requires the Attorney General to prescribe regulations on how the required label is printed. Under the DEFINITION and Example 6, requiring rulemaking counts as participation, because the rulemaking process lets people outside the government take part. The tempting 'No' reading treats the section as only a criminal ban with no process for outsiders, but that misses the rulemaking clause.
opus.s: printed in such manner as may be provided in regulations prescribed by the Attorney General
opus.b:
1. **The tempting reading.** This looks like a plain criminal ban on communications by organizations the Board has labeled Communist, with no hearing, comment period, or advisory body. That would suggest "No."
2. **Why it fails.** The required label must be printed "in such manner as may be provided in regulations prescribed by the Attorney General." Under the DEFINITION, requiring rulemaking counts as "Yes." Example 6 says the same about a grant of authority to issue regulations, because notice-and-comment rulemaking brings in the public. A single regulation clause is a thin basis, so my confidence is moderate.

qwen_chat.w: This section imposes labeling requirements on organizations already determined to be Communist by a final order. It does not involve the federal government consulting with or coordinating with outside parties before making a decision. The determination has already been made, and the section only dictates how that status must be disclosed in communications. Therefore, it does not meet the definition of participation.
qwen_chat.s: It shall be unlawful for any organization with respect to which there is in effect a final order of the Board determining it to be a Communist organization... to transmit or cause to be transmitted... any publication... unless such publication... bears the following... ‘Disseminated by... an organization determined by final order of the Subversive Activities Control Board to be a Communist... organization’
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the requirement for organizations to label their publications or broadcasts constitutes a form of public participation or transparency. However, this is a regulatory compliance requirement imposed on private entities, not a mechanism for those entities (or the public) to consult with or influence a federal decision-making process. The definition of participation requires the federal government to consult or coordinate with outsiders *before* making a decision. Here, the "decision" (the final order determining an organization is Communist) has already been made by the Board, and the section merely mandates how that determination must be disclosed in subsequent communications. There is no advisory role, comment period, hearing, or consultation involved in this specific section.
